shape: Fields follow wip/team/LEDGER_DESIGN.md (side/ledger-design, commit 22d5b83). An account made from a preset copies name, type and cur, takes preset = the preset id, and for cards starts with inFull and payDay as given here.
how_to_use: Names only, no bank connection. Show the types in the order of type_order. Inside a type, show the presets with first:true, then 'More', then the rest, then the entry with other:true, which lets the person type a name. 'for' is the one line shown under the name. 'owed' is true when the account is money owed (card, paylater, loan); it follows from type and is here only to save a lookup. payDay is null in every preset: the day differs per person, so ask for it. inFull is true for every card: ask 'Do you pay it all each month?' and, if not, make the second account 'that card, older balance' (type loan) as the ledger design says. 'statement' is an optional hint for the statements lane.

notes: first:true gives 19 names across six types for the first screen of each type: at most five per type.

payDay is the day of the month a card, pay-later plan or loan is due. A person with several pay-later plans on different days needs one account per plan, or the account's payDay left empty and each instalment entered as a bill on its own date.
The ledger design has no field for a card's statement cut-off day. Real cards have one (PH_ACCOUNTS.md, section 5, point 1). Until it exists, ask only for the due day.

Wise, Payoneer and PayPal are ewallet with cur USD and are shown beside Total until the money is brought home (convert). The ledger's freelancer test persona types Payoneer as bank; either type gives the same numbers.
Paluwagan is not a preset. Default: the contribution is a bill each pay day and the payout is 'Other money in'. See PH_ACCOUNTS.md section 5.
Order inside a type follows PH_ACCOUNTS.md: by how widely used, as far as today's sources show. Bank order is by size, not by customer count.
